    Node workflow

    Build the workflow behind the network: group tasks, make major tasks, connect them. Everything you do here shows on the Project Network.

    WORKFLOW NODES

    Task workflow

    The project name on the left is a node with a branch to each task, like the ring. Every node is a task; its rows V1, V2, V3… are its dated sessions. ☑ Select several nodes and ⬚ Group them (Ctrl+G) like a Blender node group: collapse it with ▾ and it works as one node you can connect. ＋ Major task panel is a group that is also a real major task: drag task nodes into it: the panel becomes a real major task and everything you drop in is filed under it in Project tasks, the Work timeline and the ring. On any node, ★ turns it into a major task panel and ⇲ merges it into another node as a correction (a new version). Grey wires show what sits under what; drag from a node’s right dot to another node to draw a connection — it is a real link that also appears on the ring (✕ removes it in both places). On a phone you can also tap the right dot, then tap the node to connect to. Drag a header to move a node; pinch (or hold Ctrl and scroll) to zoom. Tap a version to jump to it on the Project Network.

    Data

    Changes are saved automatically to this browser and a separate local recovery copy. Sign in with the sync button in the top bar to sync the full planner to your account across devices. Use Export data for an offline backup file before clearing browser data.

    How this planner works

    Now & Next

    The main panel shows the task happening right now with a live countdown and controls. When no task is active, quick-start buttons let you begin a focus session on the spot — no scheduled task required. When a task finishes, the scheduler moves on to the next scheduled task automatically.

    Building the day

    Click any empty spot on the timeline to add a task. Click an existing task to edit it, assign it to a project log, delete it, or — if it was skipped or never got started — carry it forward to tomorrow instead of losing it.

    Day / Week

    Switch views at the top. Week shows Monday–Friday at a glance with its own goals and a review note. Use "Add to day" next to a weekly goal to drop it straight into that day's top priorities.

    Priorities

    Three priority slots per day for what actually matters. Drag the grip on the left of a priority to move it up or down the list, or press Alt+↑ / Alt+↓ while typing in it. The Unfinished window beside today's structure holds tasks and assignments with a completion date: anything overdue, due today or due tomorrow shows up under your three priorities as extra rows (4, 5) until you tick it off. The three priority slots themselves belong to one day only. Use Project logs to record notes and work events.

    Project log

    A timestamped comment feed, like a Discord server. Each message is stamped with the time you sent it and filed under a channel (use + Channel to add one per project). Filter by channel for the day you are viewing, or open the full log (speech-bubble icon in the top bar) to browse every project across all days. Messages always post to today. Click the Project log title to minimise or expand it. It works like a diary: you can edit or delete a message only during the first minute after sending; after that it is locked.

    Calendar

    The calendar icon opens a month view. Worked days are filled in; hover a date to see the tasks you completed and your total hours (clock in/out if you used it, otherwise the sum of completed blocks). Click a date to open that day. On touch screens, tap once to preview, then use Open day. Use the suitcase icon to mark leave days, or the starburst icon to mark holidays; use the calendar icon to mark custom weekend days. Click dates to toggle each mark. The target icon jumps back to the current month. Time worked past 5pm is tracked separately as overtime: it is worked out from your clock-out (or typed into the Overtime box under the clock to override it), shown in red on each calendar day, and totalled per week and per month.

    Unfinished window

    Any task you pause or skip is moved into the Unfinished window next to Today's structure, from any day, and stays there until you tick it as completed (or resume or delete it on the timeline). Your dated tasks and assignments live in the same window. Click a task's title to open it; on narrow screens the window sits above the timeline and can be minimised.

    Overtime & task types

    If a task reaches its planned end and you haven't pressed Complete, it isn't closed for you: it is given another 15 minutes, and another, until you mark it complete. Each extension, and the final planned-versus-actual time, is written to that task's project log. A task still running when the day ends is moved to the Unfinished window. Use the pencil beside Type in the task form to add, rename or remove task types (breaks are never counted as work).

    Reminders

    The gear icon opens break, water, posture and eye-rest reminders, plus the option to enable browser notifications and the in-app chime.

    Your data

    Changes are saved automatically to this browser and a separate local recovery copy. If you sign in with the sync button in the top bar, the planner also syncs to your account across devices. Export a JSON backup from the gear icon before clearing browser data or as an extra offline backup.

    Edit project names, numbers & colours
    Edit each project name, its short number and colour. The number badge uses the project colour and appears on assigned tasks.
